newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli mutual funds' assets up 17 pct in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Israeli mutual funds' assets up 17 pct in 1997.

text.p: Assets controlled by Israeli mutual funds rose 17 percent in the first four months of 1997 to 15.88 billion shekels at the end of 1996, the Meitav investment house said on Tuesday.
An index calculated by Meitav reflecting the funds' returns rose 11.6 percent in the first third of the year, accounting for part of the increase in assets.
The increase was also due to a net inflow of 735 million shekels into the funds during this period after three years of heavy withdrawals by investors.

The funds during this period reported positive real yields across the board but stock funds did particularly well as the benchmark Mishtanim index of top 100 shares rose 20.9 percent in the January-April period while the Maof 25 index gained 21.2 percent.
